old.name: Garnatxa Negra (Empordà red)
old.hook: Black Grenache off slate and tramuntana — the workhorse red of Cap de Creus country.
old.text: Black Grenache off slate and tramuntana — the workhorse red of Cap de Creus country. €€ Garnatxa Negra (lledoner negre) is the leading black variety of DO Empordà (recognised 1975), grown on llicorella/slate soils on the Pyrenean and Cap de Creus flanks; warm, ripe-fruited, often blended with Carinyena. Martín Faixó grows it on Cap de Creus slate near Cadaqués. Producers: Martín Faixó (Perafita / Cadac labels, Cadaqués) · Espelt Viticultors (Vilajuïga) · Vinyes dels Aspres (Cantallops)

old_also.name: Carinyena / Samsó (Empordà)
old_also.hook: The drought-hardy old-vine red the Empordà builds its structure on.
old_also.text: The drought-hardy old-vine red the Empordà builds its structure on. €€ Carinyena (Samsó) is the Empordà's other principal variety, prized for old, low-yielding bush vines; resists drought and gives high total acidity and structure. Often co-planted/blended with Garnatxa. Cap de Creus monks grew vines here from the Middle Ages; phylloxera hit in 1879. Producers: Espelt Viticultors · Vinyes dels Aspres · Empordàlia

old.name: Lledoner / Garnatxa Blanca & Roig (white & grey)
old.hook: The pale Garnatxas — white lledoner and the rare red-berried lledoner roig.
old.text: The pale Garnatxas — white lledoner and the rare red-berried lledoner roig. €€ DO Empordà grows the full Garnatxa family: white (lledoner blanc), grey, and the red-berried lledoner roig recognised by its coloured skins. Used in fresh dry whites/rosats and in the sweet vi dolç. Espelt bottles a Lledoner rosat listed by DO Empordà. Producers: Espelt Viticultors (Lledoner rosat) · Martín Faixó (Perafita whites, Cadaqués) · Empordàlia

old.name: Garnatxa de l'Empordà (vi dolç)
old.hook: The DO's fortified jewel — sun-dried Garnatxa stopped with spirit, 14–20% alcohol.
old.text: The DO's fortified jewel — sun-dried Garnatxa stopped with spirit, 14–20% alcohol. €€–€€€ (500ml) A traditional fortified sweet wine of DO Empordà (DO recognised 1975; renamed DO Empordà 2006). Min. 90% Garnatxa (lledoner blanc, grey, or red lledoner roig), grapes over-ripened and sun-dried after harvest (straw-wine method), fermentation halted with grape spirit to retain natural sugar; jammy, spiced, oxidative. Drink with desserts or aged cheese. Producers: Espolla (Celler Cooperatiu d'Espolla) · Mas Estela (Estela Dolç) · Empordàlia

old.name: Cremat (rom cremat)
old.hook: Flamed Caribbean rum, coffee and cinnamon — the havaneres night in a clay pot.
old.text: Flamed Caribbean rum, coffee and cinnamon — the havaneres night in a clay pot. € (a glass, festival/bar) Dark rum heated with sugar, cinnamon, lemon peel and roasted coffee beans, then flamed and stirred until ~a third of the alcohol burns off (~10 min), doused with brewed coffee, served hot. Roots in 19th-c. Catalan–Cuba trade; bound to the havaneres sea-shanty tradition. Heartland is Calella de Palafrugell (Cantada d'Havaneres since 1966, Port-Bo trio); reaches Cadaqués and the coast in summer. Producers: Not bottled — made tableside at havaneres nights and Costa Brava taverns

old.name: Ratafia (IGP Ratafia Catalana)
old.hook: Green-walnut and herb digestif from the farmhouse mortar — drunk after the meal.
old.text: Green-walnut and herb digestif from the farmhouse mortar — drunk after the meal. €€ (700ml) Catalan herbal liqueur protected as IGP Ratafia Catalana: unripe green walnuts (picked before the shell hardens) macerated with rosemary, thyme, sage, oregano and many other herbs/flowers for a minimum of 40 days, then often aged ~3 months in wood. Sweet, tannic, dark; served as a digestif, classically with carquinyolis. Producers: Numerous Empordà/Girona family and small producers (e.g. Ratafia de l'Ermità)

old_also.name: elBulli (Cala Montjoi, Roses)
old_also.neighborhood: Cala Montjoi cove, Roses (~30 min by road along the coast from Cadaqués)
tags: Timed museum tickets via the elBulli Foundation; the road into Cala Montjoi is rough
old_also.why: Ferran Adrià's restaurant — three Michelin stars (third in 1997), World's Best multiple times — closed 30 July 2011; reopened 2023 as elBulli1846, a museum/archive of culinary creativity To order: Nothing to eat — it is now a museum (elBulli1846); the local link is that Compartir's chefs trained here NOT a restaurant any more — included only as the gravitational context for Cadaqués cooking. Do not send anyone expecting dinner.
